Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich zirconate with Zr(IV) fully oxidized, so it should resist oxidation at LiCoO2 near 4 V and is not reducible by Li6PS5Cl. Its wide gap and high Li content should keep Li-ion transport at the interface with a low interfacial penalty. Zirconate oxides are established LiCoO2 coatings.

Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich aluminosilicate whose Al3+ and Si4+ cations are fully oxidized and not reducible by Li6PS5Cl. Its orthosilicate tetrahedra should resist oxidation at LiCoO2 near 4 V, and its high Li content should support Li-ion transport across the interface, so a low interfacial penalty is plausible. The silicate family has not been tested yet.

Li6Si2O7 is a Li-rich silicate with fully oxidized Si(IV) and saturated oxo-anions, so it should resist oxidation at LiCoO2 near 4 V and is not reducible by Li6PS5Cl. Its high Li content should support Li-ion transport across the interface, which may keep the interfacial penalty low.

Li8SiO6 is a Li-rich orthosilicate with Si(IV) fully oxidized and saturated oxo-anions, so it should resist oxidation at LiCoO2 near 4 V. Its Li-rich oxide chemistry avoids reduction by Li6PS5Cl, and its high Li content should keep Li-ion transport across the interface, giving a low interfacial penalty. Silicates have not been tested in an available candidate yet.

LiZr2(PO4)3 is a NASICON-type phosphate with Zr(IV) fully oxidized and a wide band gap. Its Zr4+ centers resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl better than Ti4+ analogs, and the phosphate framework should resist oxidation at LiCoO2 near 4 V. The Li-ion-conducting framework may also keep the interfacial penalty low.
